decisions.topic: FK-existence validation for employeeId (missing capability #1 flagged by codebase-explorer)
decisions.decision: APPROVED direction: generalize into the shared master-data machine as a new field-descriptor property, e.g. `validateExists: { table: 'resources', column: 'employee_id' }`, checked in masterDataRouter.js's POST/PATCH handlers (service layer, before insert/update) — not a bespoke resource-cost-only code path, and not pushed down as a bare DB foreign-key constraint alone. Mirror the same descriptor in mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js so add_resource_cost/update_resource_cost reject an unknown employeeId before ever reaching the DB, giving a clean MCP-level error rather than surfacing a raw FK-violation/constraint error to the tool caller.
decisions.rationale: database.md: 'Validate foreign keys exist at the service layer, not the route handler' (the generic router factory *is* the service layer here — one shared check point, not one per table). CLAUDE.md §1 Simplicity First / Minimal Impact: a generalized descriptor extends the existing generic-factory pattern that already drives every other master-data table, instead of forking resource_cost onto its own hand-written route file. This also correctly distinguishes it from modules.practiceId, which is a documented, deliberate exception (unvalidated) — resource_cost.employeeId must NOT reuse that precedent, per the task's explicit requirement.
decisions.risk_if_ignored: A bespoke, one-off validation block hand-written inside a resource-cost-specific route handler would fork the generic-router abstraction the very first time a second table needs FK validation (e.g. resource_deployment likely also references resources), duplicating logic instead of extending the shared point once.

decisions.topic: Live-lookup (non-stored) response fields employeeName/employeeDesignation (missing capability #2 flagged by codebase-explorer)
decisions.decision: APPROVED direction: generalize into the shared master-data machine as a new field-descriptor kind, e.g. `lookup: { table: 'resources', on: 'employee_id', column: 'name'|'designation' }`, resolved via a join in the GET list/GET one queries (or a follow-up batched lookup query) and reflected by toResponse()/validateBody() treating a `lookup` field as read-only/non-persisted (never included in INSERT/UPDATE column lists, never accepted from request body even if the caller sends it). Do not persist employeeName/employeeDesignation as columns on resource_cost under any circumstance — that is the one hard rule from the business requirement (avoids drift from the Resources table).
decisions.rationale: database.md's naming/column conventions assume real stored columns; a computed/joined field is a genuine first-of-its-kind case in this codebase (as the codebase-explorer correctly flagged) and deserves a first-class, reusable descriptor rather than a resource-cost-only SQL join hardcoded into masterDataRouter.js's generic GET handlers. Keeping it inside the shared factory (parameterized by the descriptor) preserves the 'one factory drives every table' architecture instead of introducing a second, parallel GET-handler code path only for this table.
decisions.risk_if_ignored: A one-off join hardcoded into the generic GET list/GET one handlers, gated by `table.tableName === 'resource_cost'` or similar, would be exactly the kind of inappropriate coupling this review stage exists to catch — the generic factory would silently grow table-specific branches instead of a declarative extension point.

decisions.rationale: Reuses the existing 'number' type path in masterDataSchema.js's validateBody as-is. Adding cross-field business-rule enforcement here would be scope creep beyond what was asked.

flags_for_tech_lead_and_system_engineer: The two new field-descriptor kinds (validateExists, lookup) are genuinely new surface area on the shared master-data machine, not just this feature's schema — Tech Lead (2.5) and System Engineer (3.3) should design their exact shape once, generally enough that resource_deployment (which will very plausibly also need an employeeId FK + live lookup, per its own name-only-placeholder sibling status) doesn't need a third variant later.

Confirm whether the FK-existence check (validateExists) should run as a single extra bound-parameter query before insert/update (simplest, matches 'service layer' wording literally) versus relying on a DB-level foreign key constraint on resource_cost.employee_id referencing resources.employee_id and mapping its violation to a clean 422 error. Either is architecturally acceptable; recommend the DB-level FK constraint (belt) plus the service-layer pre-check (suspenders, for a clean error message) rather than either alone, since resources.employee_id is already uniquely constrained (0012) and can be a valid FK target.

summary: Reviewed the Business Analyst's FEAT-5 brief and the codebase-explorer's mapping of the master-data subsystem against this project's standing conventions (CLAUDE.md, database.md, api.md, frontend.md). The core requirement does not fit the existing generic master-data pattern unmodified, as both prior stages correctly identified — it needs two genuinely new capabilities: (1) FK-existence validation for employeeId against resources.employee_id, and (2) non-persisted, join-resolved response fields (employeeName/employeeDesignation) that must never drift from the Resources table. Both are approved to be added as new, reusable field-descriptor kinds on the shared master-data machine (backend/src/masterDataTables.js + mirrored mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js), generalized so future tables (notably resource_deployment, a sibling name-only placeholder that will plausibly need the same pattern) can reuse them, rather than as bespoke resource-cost-only code paths in masterDataRouter.js/masterDataSchema.js — the latter would be exactly the kind of inappropriate coupling and pattern-duplication this review stage exists to reject. offshoreCost/onsiteCost need no new capability (ordinary independent optional number fields, no cross-field enforcement added). Frontend labeling and the 0013 migration approach are approved as specified, following the 0012 precedent exactly. No blocking findings; verdict PASS. This is a read-only architecture review — no application code, schema, or migration was created or edited in this stage; those belong to the Solution Architect (3), System Engineer (3.3), and Developer (4) stages that follow.
